nodes.title: Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
nodes.statement: For every number field $K$, every nontrivial zero of its Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_K(s)$ has real part $\tfrac12$.

nodes.title: Dirichlet GRH
nodes.statement: For every primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$, every nontrivial zero of $L(s,\chi)$ has real part $\tfrac12$.

nodes.title: Riemann Hypothesis
nodes.statement: Every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(s)$ has real part $\tfrac12$.

nodes.title: Small Miller witnesses
nodes.statement: Every odd composite integer $n$ has a Miller–Rabin compositeness witness at most $2(\log n)^2$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

nodes.title: Deterministic primality testing
nodes.statement: Miller’s deterministic test decides whether an input integer is prime in time polynomial in the number of bits of the input.
nodes.status: AKS also proved unconditional deterministic polynomial-time primality testing.

nodes.title: Small quadratic nonresidues
nodes.statement: For every odd prime $p$, the least quadratic nonresidue modulo $p$ is $O((\log p)^2)$.

nodes.title: Fast square roots modulo primes
nodes.statement: Given an odd prime $p$ and a quadratic residue $a$, a square root of $a$ modulo $p$ can be found deterministically in time polynomial in $\log p$.

nodes.title: Construct irreducible polynomials
nodes.statement: Given a prime $p$ and a positive degree $d$, a deterministic algorithm produces a degree-$d$ irreducible polynomial over $\mathbb F_p$ in time polynomial in $d$ and $\log p$.

nodes.title: Deterministic finite-field construction
nodes.statement: Given a prime $p$ and positive integer $d$, an explicit presentation of the finite field $\mathbb F_{p^d}$ can be constructed deterministically in time polynomial in $d$ and $\log p$.

nodes.title: Ternary Goldbach
nodes.statement: Every odd integer greater than five is a sum of three primes.
nodes.status: Helfgott proved the full theorem unconditionally.

nodes.title: Euclidean ideal classes
nodes.statement: If the ring of integers has infinitely many units and its ideal class group is cyclic, each generating ideal class is Euclidean.

nodes.title: Euclidean algorithms in number fields
nodes.statement: The ring of integers of a number field with class number one and infinitely many units admits a Euclidean algorithm.

nodes.title: Ray class graphs expand
nodes.statement: Let $K$ have fixed degree, and let $Q$ be its absolute discriminant times the modulus norm. For each fixed $B>2$, the narrow ray-class Cayley graphs generated by prime ideals of prime norm up to $(\log Q)^B$ and their inverses have a uniform spectral gap for sufficiently large $Q$.

nodes.title: Ordinary isogeny graphs expand
nodes.statement: Ordinary elliptic curves over $\mathbb F_q$ with the same point count and isomorphic geometric endomorphism rings form an expander graph using prime-degree isogenies of degree at most $(\log(4q))^B$ for fixed $B>2$ and sufficiently large $q$.

nodes.title: Effective Chebotarev
nodes.statement: Fix a finite Galois extension $L/K$ with group $G$ and a conjugacy class $C$. The count of unramified prime ideals of norm at most $x$ with Frobenius in $C$ is $$\frac{|C|}{|G|}\operatorname{Li}(x)+O_{L/K}(\sqrt{x}\log x).$$

nodes.title: Prime counts in residue classes
nodes.statement: Fix a modulus $q$ and a residue $a$ coprime to $q$. The number $\pi(x;q,a)$ of primes at most $x$ congruent to $a$ modulo $q$ satisfies $$\pi(x;q,a)=\frac{\operatorname{Li}(x)}{\varphi(q)}+O_q(\sqrt{x}\log x).$$

nodes.title: Dirichlet’s theorem
nodes.statement: If $q\ge 1$ and $\gcd(a,q)=1$, the progression $a,a+q,a+2q,\ldots$ contains infinitely many primes.

nodes.title: First prime in a residue class
nodes.statement: If $q\ge 2$ and $\gcd(a,q)=1$, the first prime congruent to $a$ modulo $q$ is less than $2(q\log q)^2$.

nodes.title: Prime race distributions
nodes.statement: For any fixed modulus and list of reduced residue classes, the normalized errors in their prime counts have a joint limiting distribution on a logarithmic scale.

nodes.title: Sharper prime counts
nodes.statement: Let $\pi(x)$ count primes at most $x$ and use the principal-value logarithmic integral $\operatorname{Li}(x)$. For every $x\ge 2657$, $$|\pi(x)-\operatorname{Li}(x)|<\frac{\sqrt{x}\log x}{8\pi}.$$

nodes.title: Sum of reciprocal primes
nodes.statement: Let $B_1$ be the Meissel–Mertens constant. For $x\ge 13.5$, $$\left|\sum_{p\le x}\frac1p-\log\log x-B_1\right|<\frac{3\log x+4}{8\pi\sqrt{x}}.$$

nodes.title: Bounds on prime gaps
nodes.statement: The gap from a prime $p$ to the next prime is $O(\sqrt p\log p)$.

nodes.title: Möbius cancellation
nodes.statement: For each $\varepsilon>0$, the partial sums of the Möbius function satisfy $$\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)=O_\varepsilon(x^{1/2+\varepsilon}).$$

sources.label: Soundararajan, partial sums of the Möbius function
Hurst, computations of the Mertens function

nodes.title: A divisor-sum criterion
nodes.statement: For every positive integer $n$, let $\sigma(n)$ be the sum of its positive divisors and $H_n=\sum_{j=1}^n 1/j$. Then $$\sigma(n)\le H_n+e^{H_n}\log H_n.$$

nodes.title: Density of primitive roots
nodes.statement: For each fixed nonsquare integer $g\ne -1$, the primes $p$ for which $g$ generates $(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times$ have an explicit positive density among all primes.

nodes.title: Longest repeating decimals
nodes.statement: About $37.4\%$ of primes $p$ have a repeating block of length $p-1$ in the decimal expansion of $1/p$. For example, $1/7=0.\overline{142857}$.

nodes.title: Consecutive primes with primitive root 2
nodes.statement: For every positive integer $m$, there are $m$ consecutive primes for which $2$ is a primitive root modulo each prime.

nodes.title: Bound Dirichlet L-values at 1
nodes.statement: For a large negative fundamental discriminant $D$, let $\chi_D$ be its quadratic character. Then $L(1,\chi_D)$ is bounded below and above by positive constant multiples of $1/\log\log|D|$ and $\log\log|D|$, respectively.

sources.label: Lamzouri, Li and Soundararajan, class-number bounds

nodes.title: Bounds on quadratic class numbers
nodes.statement: For negative fundamental discriminants $D$ of large absolute value, the class number $h(D)$ satisfies $$\frac{\sqrt{|D|}}{\log\log|D|}\ll h(D)\ll \sqrt{|D|}\log\log|D|.$$

sources.label: Lamzouri, Li and Soundararajan, class-number bounds

nodes.title: Class-group exponent dividing two
nodes.statement: An imaginary quadratic field whose ideal class group has exponent dividing $2$ has absolute discriminant at most $5{,}460$.

nodes.title: Euler’s 65 idoneal numbers
nodes.statement: There are exactly $65$ positive integers $n$ for which the quadratic order of discriminant $-4n$ has class group of exponent dividing $2$. The largest is $1{,}848$.

nodes.title: Small prime ideals generate class groups
nodes.statement: The ideal class group of a number field of absolute discriminant $D$ is generated by prime ideals of norm at most $12(\log D)^2$.

nodes.title: A cubic class group has 2-rank 20
nodes.statement: The class group of the totally real cubic subfield of the $2$-division field of Elkies’s $2006$ elliptic curve has $2$-rank exactly $20$.

nodes.title: Elkies’s curve has rank 28
nodes.statement: The group of rational points of Elkies’s $2006$ elliptic curve has Mordell–Weil rank exactly $28$.

nodes.title: Lower bounds for root discriminants
nodes.statement: As the degree of a number field $K$ grows, its root discriminant $|\operatorname{disc} K|^{1/[K:\mathbb Q]}$ has lower limit at least $8\pi e^\gamma\approx 44.763$, where $\gamma$ is Euler’s constant.

sources.label: Hajir and Maire, discriminant bounds in towers

nodes.title: Finite unramified towers
nodes.statement: A number field of root discriminant below $8\pi e^\gamma\approx 44.763$ has no infinite unramified tower.

nodes.title: Common complex zeros in Arthur–Merlin
nodes.statement: Deciding whether a system of integer-coefficient polynomials has a common complex zero belongs to $\mathrm{AM}$, the Arthur–Merlin class of randomized verification protocols.

nodes.title: Resultant vanishing in Arthur–Merlin
nodes.statement: For a square system of homogeneous polynomials with integer coefficients, deciding whether the multivariate resultant vanishes belongs to $\mathrm{AM}$.

nodes.title: Short intervals in residue classes
nodes.statement: There are absolute constants $x_0,C,c>0$ such that, for $x\ge x_0$, $\gcd(a,q)=1$, and $C\varphi(q)\sqrt{x}\log x\le h\le x$, the interval $(x,x+h]$ contains at least $ch/(\varphi(q)\log x)$ primes congruent to $a$ modulo $q$.

nodes.title: Prime counts with growing moduli
nodes.statement: Let $\psi(x;q,a)$ be the count of prime powers up to $x$ congruent to $a$ modulo $q$, weighted by $\log p$ for powers of $p$. Uniformly for $x\ge2$ and $\gcd(a,q)=1$, $$\psi(x;q,a)=\frac{x}{\varphi(q)}+O(\sqrt{x}\log^2(qx)).$$

sources.label: Grenié and Molteni, Theorem 1.1, cyclotomic case

nodes.title: Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem
nodes.statement: For every $A>0$ there is $B>0$ such that, after taking the largest weighted counting error among coprime residue classes for each modulus, the sum of those errors over $q\le\sqrt{x}/(\log x)^B$ is $O_A(x/(\log x)^A)$.
nodes.status: Also proved unconditionally by Bombieri and Vinogradov.

nodes.title: Primes between consecutive cubes
nodes.statement: For every sufficiently large positive integer $n$, there is a prime strictly between $n^3$ and $(n+1)^3$.

sources.label: Carneiro, Milinovich and Soundararajan, prime-gap estimate

nodes.status: Also follows from Ingham’s unconditional bounds.

nodes.title: Counting squarefree integers
nodes.statement: For every $\varepsilon>0$, the number of positive integers at most $x$ indivisible by any prime square is $6x/\pi^2+O_{\varepsilon}(x^{11/35+\varepsilon})$.

sources.label: Liu, On the distribution of squarefree numbers
Mossinghoff, Oliveira e Silva and Trudgian, §1

nodes.title: Sharp bounds on zeta moments
nodes.statement: For each fixed real $k\ge0$, the average of $|\zeta(1/2+it)|^{2k}$ over $T\le t\le2T$ is $O_k((\log T)^{k^2})$ as $T$ grows.

sources.label: Harper, Sharp conditional bounds for moments

nodes.title: Primitive root counts as the base grows
nodes.statement: Let $g$ be a nonsquare integer other than $-1$. The number of primes $p\le x$ for which $g$ is a primitive root is asymptotic to $A(g)\pi(x)$, where $A(g)$ is Artin’s density for $g$. This holds even when $g$ varies with $x$, provided $\log x/\log\log(2|g|)\to\infty$.

nodes.title: First prime generated by a given base
nodes.statement: For any nonsquare integer $g\ne-1$, the smallest prime $p_g$ for which $g$ is a primitive root satisfies $p_g=O((\log(2|g|))^{19})$, with an absolute constant.

nodes.title: Average first prime for a primitive root
nodes.statement: For an integer $g$ other than $-1$ or a square, let $p_g$ be the least prime for which $g$ is a primitive root. The mean of $p_g$ over such $g$ with $|g|\le X$ tends to $$\sum_{p}\varphi(p-1)\prod_{r<p}\left(1-\frac{\varphi(r-1)}r\right),$$ where $p$ and $r$ range over primes.

nodes.title: Small primitive roots
nodes.statement: The least positive integer that generates the nonzero residues modulo a prime $p$ is $O((\log p)^6)$.

nodes.title: Find the least primitive root
nodes.statement: Given a prime $p$ and the prime factorization of $p-1$, the least positive primitive root modulo $p$ can be found deterministically in time polynomial in $\log p$.

nodes.title: Factoring from Euler’s totient
nodes.statement: Given $n$ and its Euler totient $\varphi(n)$, the prime factorization of $n$ can be computed deterministically in time polynomial in $\log n$. Computing $\varphi(n)$ from the factorization also takes polynomial time.

nodes.title: Factoring over special prime fields
nodes.statement: Degree-$d$ polynomials over $\mathbb F_p$ can be factored deterministically in time polynomial in $d$ and $\log p$ when the largest prime factor of $p-1$ is at most a fixed power of $\log p$.

sources.label: Shoup, Smoothness and Factoring Polynomials over Finite Fields

nodes.title: Class groups of exponent dividing eight
nodes.statement: There are exactly 1,046 imaginary quadratic fields of class-group exponent dividing $8$. Exactly 203 have exponent $4$ and 778 have exponent $8$.

sources.label: Elsenhans, Klüners and Nicolae, Theorem 2 and Table 1

nodes.title: A finite cutoff for class number 2,000
nodes.statement: Every imaginary quadratic field of class number at most $2{,}000$ has absolute discriminant at most $8{,}213{,}527{,}466$.

sources.label: Garcia, Grenié, Lee and Molteni, Equation (10)

nodes.title: Complete list through class number 2,000
nodes.statement: There are exactly $16{,}453{,}493$ imaginary quadratic fields of class number at most $2{,}000$. The largest absolute discriminant among them is $1{,}062{,}350{,}083$.

sources.label: Garcia, Grenié, Lee and Molteni, Table 1

nodes.title: A cubic class group has 2-rank 22
nodes.statement: The class group of the cubic subfield of the $2$-division field of Elkies’s curve $E_{27}$ has $2$-rank exactly $22$. The cubic field has one real embedding and one pair of complex embeddings.

sources.label: Klagsbrun, Sherman and Weigandt, Theorem 4 and §5.5

nodes.title: Another Elkies curve has rank 27
nodes.statement: The group of rational points on Elkies’s curve $E_{27}$ has Mordell–Weil rank exactly $27$.

nodes.title: Five curves have ranks 20 through 24
nodes.statement: For each $r\in\{20,21,22,23,24\}$, the specific elliptic curve $E_r$ in Klagsbrun, Sherman and Weigandt’s Theorem 5 has Mordell–Weil rank exactly $r$ over $\mathbb Q$.

sources.label: Klagsbrun, Sherman and Weigandt, Theorem 5 and Appendix A

nodes.title: Fast random walks on ray class graphs
nodes.statement: For these narrow ray-class Cayley graphs with sufficiently large $Q$, a walk of $O(\log |G|/\log\log Q)$ steps from any vertex reaches a fixed subset $S$ with probability at least $|S|/(2|G|)$, where $G$ is the ray class group and $Q$ is the absolute discriminant times the modulus norm.

nodes.title: Discrete logs across comparable curves
nodes.statement: If a discrete-log algorithm works on a fraction $\mu>0$ of the curves in one of these isogeny graphs, a randomized reduction solves discrete logs on any curve in the same graph with expected overhead polynomial in $\log q$ times $1/\mu$.

nodes.title: Expanders on the units modulo an integer
nodes.statement: For fixed $B>2$ and large modulus $m$, the graph on $(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^\times$ generated by multiplication by primes $p\leq(\log m)^B$ coprime to $m$ and their inverses is an expander.

sources.label: Jao, Miller and Venkatesan, example after Corollary 1.3

nodes.title: Small imaginary quadratic fields have finite towers
nodes.statement: An imaginary quadratic field $K$ with absolute discriminant $|D_K|\le 2003$ has a maximal unramified extension of finite degree over $K$.

nodes.title: Bounds on class-group torsion
nodes.statement: In a number field $K$ of degree $d\ge 2$, the number of ideal classes killed by $\ell$ is $O_{d,\ell,\varepsilon}(|D_K|^{1/2-1/(2\ell(d-1))+\varepsilon})$ for every integer $\ell\ge 1$ and every $\varepsilon>0$.

nodes.title: Smaller class-group generators
nodes.statement: If $K$ has degree $n\ge 5$ and absolute discriminant $\Delta$, the ideal class group is generated by prime ideals of norm at most $(4-1/(2n))(\log\Delta)^2$.

nodes.title: Complex dimension in Arthur–Merlin
nodes.statement: Given integer polynomial equations and an integer $d\ge 0$, deciding whether their common complex zero set has dimension at least $d$ belongs to $\mathrm{AM}$.

nodes.title: Polynomial feasibility with parameters
nodes.statement: Given polynomial equations with rational-function coefficients in formal parameters $t_1,\dots,t_m$, deciding whether they have a common solution over the algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}(t_1,\dots,t_m)$ belongs to $\mathrm{AM}$.

sources.label: Ait El Manssour et al., Theorem 1

nodes.title: Schubert coefficients in Arthur–Merlin
nodes.statement: For the classical types $A,B,C,D$, deciding whether a Schubert intersection coefficient vanishes belongs to both $\mathrm{AM}$ and $\mathrm{coAM}$. Both zero and nonzero answers admit Arthur–Merlin verification.

nodes.title: At most four primes suffice
nodes.statement: Every integer $n\ge2$ can be expressed as a sum of at most four primes.

sources.label: Pintz, Consequence of ternary Goldbach, p. 388

nodes.status: This also follows unconditionally from Helfgott’s theorem.

nodes.title: Square-root bound on binary Goldbach exceptions
nodes.statement: The number of even integers from $4$ to $X$ that fail to be sums of two primes is $O_{\varepsilon}(X^{1/2+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$.

sources.label: Hardy and Littlewood, Partitio Numerorum V

nodes.title: Two-prime sums in short intervals
nodes.statement: For each real $x\ge 2$, the interval $(x,x+123\log^2 x]$ contains an even integer that is the sum of two primes.
